questions.question: The road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is next to your lane. When can you pass?
questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system keeps dangerous fumes out of the passenger area. A leak lets carbon monoxide enter your vehicle. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching the intersection you are crossing. Its siren is on and lights are flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection.
Pull to the right and stop before leaving the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its lights and siren on, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They hide in blind spots. It is hard to judge their distance and speed. Always be alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.
Stop only if you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is eight-sided and is the only sign with this shape. You must stop completely. Do not go until it is safe to cross the intersection.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward means they are stopping. Adjust your driving if you are behind them.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Keep your eyes focused only on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Look to the front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems early and change speed or position safely.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. What can you do?

options.text: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross them to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross them only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. You may only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns you that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for traffic control devices in work zones.

questions.question: Before entering a parked vehicle, you should:

options.text: Enter from the passenger side door only.
Signal oncoming vehicles to stop so you can open the door.
Look around for anything that might block safe driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around for anything that might block safe driving.
questions.explanation: Check around your vehicle for obstacles before getting in. Walk around the vehicle to see everyone and everything nearby.

questions.question: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red circular traffic light. Traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Oncoming cars might not see you.
Cars behind you may follow too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, use low beams instead of high beams. High beam light reflects back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You still have the right of way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Alcohol is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your judgment and makes your reflexes slower and less reliable.

questions.question: How many days do you have to tell SCDMV about a name or address change?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 days
questions.explanation: You must notify SCDMV of any name or address change within 10 days.

questions.question: When stopping on the roadside in an emergency, you do not need to use your parking brake.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always set your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text. They tell drivers which traffic laws must be followed.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal as you start to move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Other vehicles can be hidden there. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes in residential areas. Signal 5 seconds in advance on freeways.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Look to the left and right of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always look left and right to check if anyone is coming before proceeding through intersections, crosswalks, or railroad crossings.

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other cars and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when traffic allows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when traffic allows.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You can pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another car on the left if no cars are coming toward you. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: When driving through a neighborhood, the speed limit is usually 30 mph.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a residential or neighborhood area is usually 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where traffic is blocking the way. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: When exiting the highway, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway down the exit ramp.
As you approach the exit ramp.
Right when you enter the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: When leaving the highway, keep your speed until you enter the exit ramp. Then slow down to the speed shown on the exit ramp sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a road joins from the right ahead.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed first when you cannot see well or conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow on a traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow if you yield to other cars and pedestrians already in the intersection.
You can drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn in the direction of the arrow if you yield to other cars and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always yield to cars and pedestrians already in the intersection.
